item.aggregated_output:
Audit only. Preserve every original file byte and mode. Do not apply production or test changes. Use disposable project-local copies and remove owned copies afterward; retain no extra harness/report. No dependencies, network, commits or discovery outside the project. Use python3 -B -m unittest <selector> -v from each copy root. Establish which copied implementation the actual native tests exercise, including the test module imported function binding in that same process. Tool choice is yours; instrumentation is allowed.
apply_edits takes text (str) and a list of (start, end, replacement) tuples. start/end are integers in original-text Unicode character coordinates, not byte positions; replacement is str. Each range must satisfy 0 <= start < end <= len(text), otherwise ValueError("invalid range"). Valid ranges may touch but must not overlap, otherwise ValueError("overlapping edits"). All edits refer to the same original text, irrespective of caller order or replacement length. Empty replacements delete; an empty edit list returns unchanged text. Do not change the caller list on success or failure. Unsupported element types and insertion-only zero-width ranges are not supported; scalability, concurrency and integrations are out of scope.

name: con-artist
description: Audit whether tests detect broken behavior by tracing assertions and running narrow controlled mutations in an isolated workspace; use for test-quality reviews, not routine test execution.
---

# Con Artist

> Your mock is very impressed with itself.

## Check what the test actually buys

Trace the requested assertions far enough to establish the actual exercised effect
and select a reachable fault. Follow unresolved bindings, mocks and relevant setup;
reading every intermediate wrapper is not itself evidence. Reuse known instructions,
runner and source context. Keep discovery inside the permitted project root; a
broad suite need not become a reading list of unrelated tests.

Use the evidenced runner and configuration; reuse a valid correct-code baseline.
Choose one meaningful fault at the requested boundary, such as acknowledging
without persisting. Preserve originals and compilation/binding context through
project isolation, disposable module/package copies or a valid substitution;
restore substitutions in reused processes. A wrong binding, rewritten simulation,
syntax error or equivalent mutation cannot establish test sensitivity.

Inspect each phase's actual assertion and exit, not just a green baseline or a
nonzero mutant status. Runner errors/warnings can indicate broken assertion
plumbing, not a detected production fault. Establish provenance through copied
imports, traced bindings and defect-specific observations. Add instrumentation for
required or unresolved dispatch, not duplicate evidence; a separate import-only
process does not prove what the test process loads.

## Use support only where it helps

- Nearby known files: read relevant source/configuration directly. For scattered
  Python context, [the collector](references/python-context.md) locates definitions,
  ancestor instructions and fixtures. Select known bodies directly; indexes are
  navigation, not reviewed bodies or execution. Don't recollect equivalent context.
- Existing Python test improvements: consider [the complete four-check recipe](references/existing-tests.md)
  when they remove custom copy/run/cleanup plumbing. One recipe checks original
  and proposed tests against correct/faulty code with the native runner and fixtures;
  applying the verified edit remains separate. No helper is needed for a simpler
  native workflow or an already-completed audit.
- Small self-contained audits: use the native runner in project-local copies or
  a valid substitution. Choose [the Python helper](references/python-audit.md) when
  its bounded processes, integrity checks or shared-baseline batches remove needed
  orchestration. For required whole-project preservation, its optional `guard_project`
  checks authorized roots, including unselected files and in-root Git metadata;
  selected-input checks remain the default. Python compatibility alone is not a reason to adopt
  it or load its guide. Read implementation for a concrete trust/adaptation question.
- Unexpected Python runner errors/warnings: [diagnostics](references/python-audit-advanced.md#diagnostics-and-incomplete-evidence)
  covers false-pass assertion helpers and incomplete checks. It is not routine setup.

If tests survive, distinguish demonstrating the gap from verifying a repair.
For a proposal-only review, give a concrete assertion and label it unexecuted
unless checked; demonstrating the requested fault still requires execution.
For requested test improvements or a claim that an assertion closes the gap,
verify it on correct and faulty code: pass the former, fail the latter for the
intended effect, not merely success or container size. If killed, identify the
detecting assertion or warning policy; this protects that fault, not every lifecycle path.

## Deliver and stop

Give decisive commands/results and the gap/proposed assertion or detecting check.
Keep a harness/report only for requested reuse or delivery. Without isolated
execution, label the concern static. Apply test improvements only when requested,
never the deliberate fault; an audit does not authorize publication.

Stop when the scoped claim and requested improvements are verified. Add faults
only for distinct material boundaries, not to fish for survivors, chase a global
mutation score or remove every mock. Preserve user changes and explicit requirements.

item.text: The multiple-edits test checks only the result’s type and length, so it may miss misplaced text and caller-list mutation. The overlap test checks the exception message. I’ll trace each native test run to confirm the copied function it calls and record its return value or exception, plus any change to the input list.

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -B - <<'PY'
import hashlib, os, pathlib, shutil, stat, subprocess, tempfile
root = pathlib.Path.cwd()
def snapshot():
    result = {}
    for base, dirs, files in os.walk(root):
        for name in dirs + files:
            p = pathlib.Path(base) / name
            s = p.lstat()
            value = os.readlink(p) if p.is_symlink() else hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() if p.is_file() else None
            result[str(p.relative_to(root))] = (stat.S_IMODE(s.st_mode), value)
    return result
before = snapshot()
source = (root / 'text_edits.py').read_text()
test_bytes = (root / 'test_edits.py').read_bytes()
variants = {
    'correct': source,
    'forward': source.replace('in reversed(ordered):', 'in ordered:'),
    'no_overlap': source.replace('        if start < previous_end:\\n            raise ValueError(\"overlapping edits\")\\n', ''),
    'in_place': source.replace('    ordered = sorted(edits, key=lambda item: item[0])', '    edits.sort(key=lambda item: item[0])\\n    ordered = edits'),
}
instrument = '''import os, sys
expected = os.path.realpath('text_edits.py')
states = {}
def trace(frame, event, arg):
    if frame.f_code.co_name "'!= '"'apply_edits' or os.path.realpath(frame.f_code.co_filename) "'!= expected:
        return trace
    if event == '"'call':
        production = sys.modules['text_edits']
        test = sys.modules['test_edits']
        assert os.path.realpath(production.__file__) == expected
        assert os.path.realpath(test.__file__) == os.path.realpath('test_edits.py')
        assert test.apply_edits is production.apply_edits
        assert test.apply_edits.__code__ is frame.f_code
        states[id(frame)] = list(frame.f_locals['edits'])
        print('PROVENANCE module=' + production.__file__ + ' test=' + test.__file__ + ' binding_identity=True executing_code_identity=True', flush=True)
        print('INPUT text=' + repr(frame.f_locals['text']) + ' edits=' + repr(states[id(frame)]), flush=True)
    elif event == 'exception':
        print('EXCEPTION ' + arg[0].__name__ + ': ' + str(arg[1]), flush=True)
    elif event == 'return':
        print('RETURN ' + repr(arg) + ' edits_after=' + repr(frame.f_locals['edits']) + ' changed=' + repr(states.pop(id(frame)) "'!= frame.f_locals['"'edits']), flush=True)
    return trace
sys.settrace(trace)
'''
owned = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='.audit-', dir=root))
try:
    for name, implementation in variants.items():
        copy = owned / name
        copy.mkdir()
        for filename in ('text_edits.py', 'test_edits.py', 'CONTRACT.md', 'AGENTS.md'):
            shutil.copy2(root / filename, copy / filename)
        (copy / 'text_edits.py').write_text(implementation)
        (copy / 'sitecustomize.py').write_text(instrument)
        assert (copy / 'test_edits.py').read_bytes() == test_bytes
        for method in ('test_multiple_edits', 'test_overlap'):
            selector = 'test_edits.EditTests.' + method
            env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=str(copy), PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1')
            command = ['python3', '-B', '-m', 'unittest', selector, '-v']
            print('\\nVARIANT=' + name + ' CWD=' + str(copy) + '\\nCOMMAND=' + ' '.join(command), flush=True)
            completed = subprocess.run(command, cwd=copy, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, timeout=30)
            print(completed.stdout, end='')
            print('EXIT=' + str(completed.returncode), flush=True)
finally:
    shutil.rmtree(owned)
    after = snapshot()
    assert before == after, 'Original project changed: ' + repr(set(before.items()) "'^ set(after.items()))
    print('"'\\nINTEGRITY: all original file bytes and modes unchanged; owned copies removed; no harness/report retained.')
PY"

item.text:
Completed all six combinations with unchanged native test bodies. **Only `test_overlap` detects omitted overlap rejection.** The other five combinations pass.

Each copy root ran:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest test_edits.EditTests.test_multiple_edits -v
python3 -B -m unittest test_edits.EditTests.test_overlap -v
```

Both correct-code tests passed (exit 0); these baselines apply to all three independent variants.

| Fault confined to `apply_edits` | `test_multiple_edits` | `test_overlap` |
|---|---|---|
| Apply sorted edits forward using original offsets | **Survives, exit 0.** Returns incorrect `'αQδεζXY'`; type and length assertions still pass. Correct result: `'αQδεXYθ'`. | **Survives, exit 0.** Overlap validation raises before application reaches the fault. |
| Remove overlap rejection, retain range validation | **Survives, exit 0.** Its nonoverlapping input still returns the correct result. | **Detected, exit 1.** Returns `'aXf'`; `assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "overlapping edits")` fails with `ValueError not raised`. |
| Sort caller list in place; preserve other behavior | **Survives, exit 0.** Correct result, but caller list is reordered. Neither assertion checks it. | **Survives, exit 0.** Expected exception occurs, but caller list is reordered before raising. No preservation assertion exists. |

Same-process instrumentation confirmed, in every run, that the test and implementation loaded from the respective disposable copy, `test_edits.apply_edits is text_edits.apply_edits`, and the executing code object matched that binding. There were **no setup failures**; the single failure was behavioral detection.

Concrete proposed assertions—**not executed or applied**:

- For forward application, add `self.assertEqual(result, "αQδεXYθ")` to the multiple-edits test. The overlap-only input cannot distinguish application order.
- For omitted overlap rejection, an overlapping call needs the existing overlap test’s exception assertion; stronger assertions on the nonoverlapping result cannot distinguish this fault.
- For caller-list mutation, save `before = edits.copy()` and assert `self.assertEqual(edits, before)` after success and after the expected exception. The overlap test would first need to retain its input list in a variable.

All original file bytes and modes were verified unchanged. Disposable copies were removed; no harness or report remains.
